label: late original-phase token right after g (also q, p)
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase at positions 4-8, peaking at t=5-6. 99% of activation mass is there, and it is essentially silent at t<=3 and in the copy phase (only weak firing at the delimiter). Inside that window the strongest modulator is the previous input token: after g the rate is 21% (9x lift) and g accounts for about 49% of mass; the top activations are mostly the step right after a g. q and p give weaker boosts, and g/q two steps back adds a little more. The predicate prev_tok in {g,q,p} at t=4..7 has about 0.51 precision and 0.61 mass recall on dev. prev_tok==g alone gives 0.90 precision but only 0.47 mass recall. There is also a weak, diffuse background over many late original-phase steps with other preceding tokens, so recall is incomplete. Position alone (t>=4 in the original phase) covers 99% of mass but has only 12% precision.
